sections.h2: Why do Flint sales hinge on condition and clear title?
sections.html:
Flint homes sell for far less than homes elsewhere in Michigan, so a seller's outcome depends on repair costs, liens and ownership history more than on the asking price. The city serves as the Genesee County seat, sits about 66 miles northwest of Detroit on the Flint River, and had an estimated 79,306 residents on July 1, 2025.

Owners can list with an agent, sell to a neighbor or investor privately, or accept an as-is cash purchase. The sections below match each route with Flint's rental ordinance, its water billing rule, county tax foreclosure and the numbers behind local values.

sections.h2: How has Flint's history shaped its housing today?
sections.html:
Fur trader Jacob Smith founded a trading post here in 1819, the village incorporated in 1855, and lumber and carriage building turned into automobile manufacturing. Buick moved to Flint, Chevrolet built its first plant here, and General Motors was founded in the city in 1908. Local GM employment peaked near 80,000 in 1978 and fell below 8,000 by 2010.

The city's population followed. It peaked near 197,000 in 1960 and measured 81,252 in the 2020 Census. The housing stock was built for that larger workforce, so a seller here is often marketing an older house to a smaller pool of buyers than the city once had.

  • Older houses can carry repair items such as roofs, wiring and plumbing that a buyer's inspector will list.
  • The Land Bank holds vacant lots and houses, so some occupied blocks sit beside empty parcels.
  • Tax foreclosure has shaped ownership, which is why parcel history is worth checking before you sell.

sections.h2: How low are Flint home values, and who owns the houses?
sections.html:
Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024 show a city where renters nearly match owners and where a median house is worth about the price of a used car.

At $53,500, a roof or a furnace can consume a large part of the equity an owner holds. This is the main reason many Flint owners compare a quick sale of the house as it stands with the delay and expense of bringing it up to retail condition.

sections.h2: Which Flint neighborhoods and landmarks matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Flint's neighborhoods are grouped around downtown, which is centered on Saginaw Street south of the river. Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District hold preserved Victorian houses just west of downtown. East of I-475, Central Park and Fairfield Village sit between the University of Michigan-Flint and Mott Community College. East Village and the College Cultural Neighborhood on the east side are described as more stable, and the west side includes Mott Park and the Woodcroft Estates.

Public schools are run by Flint Community Schools, which operates ten elementary schools, one middle school and Flint Southwestern Academy. Catholic and charter schools also serve the city. Kettering University, UM-Flint and Mott Community College are all in or beside the city's core.

sections.h2: What are Flint's rental rules, and do they affect a sale?
sections.html:
They do if the house has tenants. Flint's rental ordinance requires rental properties to be registered with the city and certified after an inspection. A December 2023 city memo put the single-family registration at a one-time $250 and the inspection at $225 every three years, and it said tenants make up nearly half of Flint households. Landlords must provide heat from October 1 through March 31.

The same memo explains a water rule that surprises owners: the city prefers water accounts in the owner's name, and unpaid water bills become a lien that can be added to the property tax bill. If you are selling a rental, confirm that the water account is paid and ask the Building and Safety Inspections Division at 810-766-7284 about the certification status. Fees change, so ask for the current schedule.

sections.h2: How does Genesee County tax foreclosure affect Flint sellers?
sections.html:
A delinquent tax bill can move a house into county tax foreclosure, and that is a real risk for owners of inherited or vacant property. The Genesee County Land Bank takes in properties through the tax foreclosure process: houses that go unsold at the public auction and are not claimed by the state or a local government are transferred from the County Treasurer to the Land Bank at the end of each calendar year.

Owners in the city can check parcel ownership through the city's property lookup, and a parcel listed under Genesee County LRC Inc or the Genesee County Treasurer is held by the Land Bank. For a seller, the lesson is simple: pay or arrange the back taxes before the foreclosure clock runs out, because a sale closed on time keeps the equity that an auction would not.

  • Check the balance with the county treasurer before you sign any sale contract.
  • Unpaid water bills can sit on the tax roll as well.
  • Ask the title company to pull liens early so surprises do not delay closing.

sections.h2: What does the Michigan transfer tax cost on a Flint house?
sections.html:
Michigan charges 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on each $500 of price (MCL 207.504 and 207.525). Sellers carry it, and the county treasurer expects payment within 15 days of the deed's delivery (MCL 207.523).

At Flint's median home value of $53,500 the two taxes add up to roughly $460, which the settlement statement will show exactly. The new owner files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the city assessor within 45 days, and the taxable value resets the following year (MCL 211.27a).

sections.h2: When does an as-is sale beat a listing in Flint?
sections.html:
A sound house on a stable block can do well with an agent, provided the buyer can pass an appraisal at a price close to the contract. When repairs would exceed the value they add, or a lien, code order or tenant dispute complicates matters, a direct purchase of the house as it stands avoids most of that friction.

  • Choose a listing when the house is move-in ready and you can wait through loan approval.
  • Choose an as-is buyer when repair quotes outrun the likely sale price.
  • Offer vacant land beside an occupied home to the owner next door, since the Land Bank sells side lots on the same logic.

Request proof of funds, read the closing date clause, and compare offers by what you keep after liens and costs.

faqs.q: Can unpaid property taxes be settled out of a Flint sale?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if the sale closes before the county finishes foreclosure. The title company pays the balance from the seller's proceeds, and the Genesee County Treasurer can confirm the payoff figure and the foreclosure timeline.

faqs.q: Do unpaid Flint water bills follow the house?
faqs.a: They can. City rules let delinquent water charges become a lien that is added to the property tax bill, so a title company will usually ask for a paid account before closing.

faqs.q: What does Flint require of a landlord?
faqs.a: Rental properties must be registered and certified after an inspection, repeated every three years, and landlords must supply heat from October 1 through March 31. Ask the Building and Safety Inspections Division for the current fees.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax would I owe at Flint's median home value?
faqs.a: About $460 on a $53,500 sale, using 55 cents per $500 for the county plus $3.75 per $500 for the state. Your settlement statement will show the exact amount.

faqs.q: What does the Genesee County Land Bank do?
faqs.a: It receives tax-foreclosed properties that fail to sell at auction, then sells houses and lots, offers side lots to neighboring owners and demolishes dangerous structures as funding allows.
